Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon in which two or more particles become correlated in such a way that the state of one particle cannot be described independently of the others, even when the particles are separated by large distances.

In other words, entangled particles are connected in such a way that their properties are linked, and measuring the state of one particle will instantaneously affect the state of the other, regardless of the distance between them.

Entanglement is a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics and has been experimentally confirmed in numerous studies. It has potential applications in quantum computing, quantum cryptography, and other areas of quantum technology.
